name: The Fort Dearborn Massacre monument (Carl Rohl-Smith, 1893), 18th Street at Calumet Avenue

function.note: A bronze group commissioned by George M. Pullman and placed near his house in 1893, near where the battle of 15 August 1812 was believed to have been fought.

built.note: Wikipedia: placed in 1893 'near the intersection of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street'; Chicago and Cook County Cemeteries: Pullman commissioned it in 1893 and it was removed in 1931.

research_note: THE FORT DEARBORN MASSACRE MONUMENT, built by T-3567 (piece 1 of T-3565, the owner's request of 2026-11-12 after a meeting with Bill Tyre). This record carries review_required because it depicts the battle of 15 August 1812 and Potawatomi people, in a work American Indian protesters objected to from the 1970s (karamanski_2004_monuments_lost_nation); the figures are built as the sculptor made them, as period sculpture, and the card says how the work was received. The fighting is not staged: this is the statue that stood on 18th Street, not the event. WHERE: the photographs put it at the east end of 18th Street's north walk, by the curve into Calumet Avenue, before the Pullman estate's 18th Street wall and just east of the stable's end (ICHi-19208 is captioned 'at Calumet Street and 18th' and shows the stable's rock-faced end at left; the Detroit Publishing view LC-D4-12552 shows it beyond the stable's hydrant at the curb). The texts disagree: the 1893 Rand, McNally guide has it 'at the foot of Eighteenth Street', the 1905 Views of Chicago and later accounts 'at Eighteenth Street and Prairie Avenue', a 1929 Tribune 'a few feet from Prairie avenue on 18th street' (all quoted on Chicagology, no source records); the photographs are followed. LATER: moved in 1931 to the Chicago Historical Society (chicagoandcook_2017_1812_massacre_site, wikipedia_fort_dearborn_massacre_monument), subtitled 'The Potawatomi Rescue' in 1972, protested in 1973, returned by the city to the Prairie Avenue district and later put into storage (karamanski_2004_monuments_lost_nation). Cameras on ICHi-19208, Taylor's 1893 view and the Detroit print, and the side-by-sides, are T-3568's (data/reference_views/fort_dearborn_massacre_monument_1893/): the pedestal matches them; the figures, joined from tapered limbs, do not yet read as Rohl-Smith's sculpture, and their match records say figure by figure where they differ. The Detroit print (LC-D4-12552, c. 1900) shows the lettered pedestal with no group on it: see its match record.

documented_range.note: Placed in 1893 and moved to the Chicago Historical Society in 1931; neither the day it was set up nor the day it was taken down is read here, so the range is the two years whole. It covers the 1904 scene and neither 1812 nor 1835.

position.symbolic_location: The north walk of E. 18th Street at its east end, where it curves into Calumet Avenue: before the Pullman estate's 18th Street wall, east of the Pullman stable's end (local E 1501.3, N -3198.76 at the base's centre).
position.note: The base's south-west corner. Placed by T-3568 through two cameras. EAST AND WEST, the Detroit print LC-D4-12552 (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08066.json, the Pullman house's camera, its heading fitted on the house at 2.4-2.6 px rms): the pedestal's centre stands at x 800 px of the 1024 px print, a bearing of 330.4 degrees from the eye, which crosses the base's centre line (N -3198.76) at E 1501.3, 4.8 m east of T-3567's place by eye (E 1496.5). NORTH AND SOUTH, ICHi-19208 (data/reference_views/fort_dearborn_massacre_monument_1893/chm_ichi_19208.json, fitted on the pedestal alone): the estate wall's foot runs behind the monument at y 775 px, 11.8 m from the eye, 4.1 m north of the base's front, against the parcel's 18th Street line at 4.7 m (prairie_1729's south edge, N -3195.5 in data/street_grid/1904.json); so the base's centre stays 3.25 m south of that line, where T-3567 set it. Good to about 1.5 m east and west (a 10 px error in the Detroit print's bearing is 0.7 m there) and 0.6 m north and south. Two things do not agree with it yet and are open in the match records: the Detroit camera, fitted on the house 80-90 m off, does not hold its foreground and draws the pedestal at about 0.57 of the size the print shows; and through ICHi-19208 the Pullman stable's draft (pullman_house_1729_prairie_ranges) stands about 6 m east of the end the print shows at its left edge. The texts disagree on the place (the 1893 Rand, McNally guide 'at the foot of Eighteenth Street'; the 1905 Views of Chicago 'at Eighteenth Street and Prairie Avenue'; all quoted on Chicagology, no source records); the photographs are followed. Rotation 359.62 degrees squares its front to 18th Street's line (bearing 89.62 degrees); the corner also moved 0.225 m north when the base's depth went from 3.3 m to 2.85 m, so that its centre stays on the line.

derivation.reason: Placed through the cameras on the Detroit print and ICHi-19208 against the 1904 street grid's parcel line; no platted corner or traced frontage carries a monument.

footprint.note: The stage base's rectangle (form.base_w_m by form.base_d_m); the generator stands the plinth, die, cap and group on its centre.

base_w_m.note: Read off ICHi-19208 at the die's plane, taking the die's front as 2.4 m (form.die_w_m): the die's body is 155 px high (y 430-585 of the side-by-side's half-size copy) on 300 px of width, the stage base 80 px, the plinth 60, the cap 35, the group about 270 over the cap. The pedestal so read is 2.7 m to the cap's top and 3.0 m to the rock's, which is the Inter Ocean's 'ten feet' (15 September 1892, quoted on Chicagology; no source record, so a check, not a citation) if its pedestal counts the rock. Width: the base reads 510 px on that 300 px die, 1.7 times it, less the nearer face's perspective (about 9.0 m against the die's 9.6 m): 3.8 m. The WBEZ account's 'eight by nine feet' (2.4 x 2.7 m, no source record) is about the die's size, not the stage the photographs show.

base_d_m.note: Fitted on J. W. Taylor's 1893 three-quarter view through its camera (data/reference_views/fort_dearborn_massacre_monument_1893/aic_taylor_1893.json, T-3568), the one picture used here that sees a side of the pedestal: fourteen corners of the base, plinth and die on the front and west faces, fitted together with the camera (level, eye free), with the base's front held at 3.8 m. The side faces read 85 px (base), 77 (plinth) and 61 (die) against fronts of 857, 596 and 546 px, and the fit gives base 2.81-2.89 m, plinth 1.74-1.85 m and die 1.51-1.69 m deep for any eye from 1.4 to 2.4 m over the walk (9.5-11.5 px rms on a die about 220 px a metre, so 0.05 m), and the plinth's and die's widths 2.73-2.75 and 2.47-2.50 m against the record's 2.8 and 2.4, inside the tolerance and left as they were. The base: 2.85 m. Replaces the reconstructed 3.3 m (the width less a margin), which the side shows 0.45 m too deep.

rock_h_m.note: The cast rock between the cap's top (y 470 px) and the figures' feet (about y 430-445) on ICHi-19208: 25-40 px, about 0.3 m.

group_h_m.note: The group with its rock, over the cap. Read off ICHi-19208 at the die's plane (the die's 155 px body is 1.25 m, form.die_h_m): the figures stand about 270 px over the cap, 2.2 m there, and the group stands about 1 m behind the die's front, which puts it at about 2.4 m, with the 0.3 m rock 2.7-2.75 m. That agrees with the 'about nine feet' Wikipedia gives (wikipedia_fort_dearborn_massacre_monument, cited for the text alone, its rights unresolved). The figures' places and poses are the generator's (generators/archetypes/monument.py FIGURES), read off ICHi-19208 and checked on Taylor's 1893 view, to about 0.2 m; faces, dress folds, feathers and the group's rear are reconstructed (L-fort-dearborn-monument-3567).

panels.note: A bronze panel on each face of the die: ICHi-19208 shows the front one (the column leaving the fort, in low relief) and Taylor's view the east side's; the Rand, McNally guide of 1893 (quoted on Chicagology, no source record) gives four. Their reliefs are not modelled. L-fort-dearborn-monument-3567

lettering.value: THE FORT DEARBORN MASSACRE / AUGUST 15, 1812 / BLACK PARTRIDGE SAVING MRS. HELM
lettering.note: Cut in the die under the front panel, three lines (ICHi-19208, y 665-695 px). Not built: no letter in this town is modelled at this size; the die's face below the panel is plain. L-fort-dearborn-monument-3567

phases.change_note: Built T-3567 (2026-11-12): the monument stands in the 1904 scene, on the new pure-Python monument archetype. Refined T-3568 (2026-11-13): the pedestal's depths read through a camera on Taylor's 1893 view (base 2.85 m, plinth 1.8, die 1.6, were 3.3, 2.3 and 1.9 reconstructed); cameras on ICHi-19208, Taylor 1893 and Detroit LC-D4-12552.
